text:
incident-bot: ALERT: ap-southeast-1 - multiple health probes silent (Route53 / internal agent). Pager triggered for SRE oncall.

lee: seeing the same. dashboards for ap-southeast-1 show probe heartbeats stopped ~10:34 UTC. no obvious spike in CPU on probe fleet.

maria: telemetry for route53 health checks shows TIMEOUTs, but the healthcheck endpoints still return 200 for a manual curl from my laptop.

sre-oncall: are these the external edge probes or internal mesh probes? any correlation with the maintenance window? @katie?

katie: no scheduled maintenance in ap-southeast-1 today. I just checked infra-calendar. This looks like a monitoring fanout/collector issue rather than backend servers failing.

netops-bot: SYSTEM: AWS provider ticket opened (case-id: AWS-932188). Provider reported "no infrastructure events detected" for the AZs in ap-southeast-1.

lee: I can still reach customer-facing endpoints from euw2 and usw2. Traffic looks normal, but synthetic checks are flapping. That suggests probe telemetry/collector.

maria: quick mitigation: suppress noisy alerts for ap-southeast-1 probe group to avoid paging storm. I'll apply a temporary suppression rule for 30m and add a sticky note.

sre-oncall: agreed. suppress alerts but keep escalations for actual 5xxs. Also enable alternate healthcheck source (remote-prober-1 in us-west) as a fallback for synthetic validation.

lee: adding a Route53 healthcheck override to use the fallback probe set now:

```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://r53-fallback.json
```

will keep TTL low until we confirm.

katie: live update: suppression in alerting system created (ID: sup-1938), expires in 30m. fallback healthchecks in progress.

maria: checked logs from collector nodes in ap-southeast-1, there's a gap in the collector service at ~10:33:45 - process respawned at 10:35:12. likely short crash loop that dropped heartbeat emission. attaching sample log snippet:

```
2026-03-15T10:33:40Z collector[pid=1421]: heartbeat send failed: write tcp 10.0.2.5:56832->10.0.5.7:443: connection reset by peer
2026-03-15T10:33:42Z collector[pid=1421]: panic: runtime error: index out of range
2026-03-15T10:35:12Z systemd[1]: collector.service: started
```

lee: that aligns with probe silence. looks like a collector bug caused temporary telemetry missing, which tripped downstream alerting.

ash: onboarding netops. we should run a quick scan for similar crashes in other regions to ensure this is isolated.

katie: running a grep across collector logs for "panic" since 00:00 UTC... so far only ap-southeast-1 shows the panic.

maria: impact summary for customers: no confirmed user-facing outage. A subset of our synthetic checks reported failures, which could have caused external monitoring providers to page. Application metrics (5xx, latency) are stable.

sre-oncall: customer impact: LOW. But follow-up required: fix collector crash, add auto-restart safeguards, and adjust alerting to differentiate probe silence vs backend errors.

lee: creating a bug in tracker: RDW-6542 "collector: bounds-check panic on heartbeat buffer". tagging infra/collector and eng-runtime.

maria: ops note: re-enabled alerts at 10:55 UTC after collector processes patched (hotfix deployed to restart logic). No further silent periods observed.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to S3 - monitoring noise / false-positive.

katie: next steps for postmortem: root cause analysis of panic, re-run load tests for collector, add per-process telemetry for quick detection, and update runbook for suppressing alerts safely. I'll own the postmortem.

ash: I'll take ownership of the follow-up remediation (collector stable rollout and blue/green for collector fleet).

lee: handing off to next oncall for the 11:00-19:00 UTC shift — @ash you're up. I'll add a brief summary in ops-handoffs channel.

ash: acknowledged. thanks. summary please include: what we did (suppress alerts, fallback healthchecks, hotfix to restart collector), customer impact (none), follow-ups (RDW-6542, postmortem owned by katie).

ash: marking this thread resolved for the active incident. if anything flares, re-open or DM. :white_check_mark:
